pending BSS+MAC identity ledger. The prepared RRB and ordinary `MlmeEnqueueForRecv`

## FT pending queue dispatch and drain prepared — 2026-11-19

Extended the uninstalled queue composer to initialize sidecar fields for every
native queue slot, reject ticket enqueue after the primary MLME queue closes,
validate stale tickets before state-machine dispatch, and release the ticket
under MacTabLock after the handler returns. Halt closes the pending ingress,
then drains detached slot tickets after RtmpOSTaskKill and before queue destroy.
PCI restart closes ingress after exclusive bRunning acquisition, drains queued
references, and reopens after the native reset sequence. Drain detaches under
Queue->Lock and releases after dropping that lock, so no Queue->Lock/MacTabLock
nesting is introduced. FT BT_REQ is ACTION_STATE_MACHINE traffic and the clone
admits it only to the primary queue; EAP queue sidecar slots are still initialized.

`check-ft-pending-enqueue.py` executes the complete enqueue clone under
ASan/UBSan in default/EAP/SNR variants and asserts handler, restart, halt, init,
close, drain and reopen ordering against pinned source. The C, Nim, insertion,
existing-peer enqueue and parser regressions pass (exit 0). Evidence:
`docs/evidence/WR1200JS-FT-PENDING-ENQUEUE-HOST-2026-11-19.json`.

## FT new-peer semantics and local regression results — 2026-11-19

Exact pinned `mgmt_entrytb.c` shows `MacTableInsertEntry` chooses the first free
WCID and appends to the MAC hash without rejecting a duplicate MAC. Thus a
first-time FT BT_REQ can create a same-MAC peer on its target BSS while another
BSS already has that address; the native global MAC lookup is ambiguous. A safe
continuation needs both target-BSS insertion and an ingress identity that cannot
be adopted by a stale queued event.

Host checks against c25283e and the current prepared scripts all exit 0:
`check-ft-parser-composition.py`, `check-ft-generation-binding.py`, and
`check-ft-enqueue-generation.py`. They cover the current uninstalled RRB parser,
FT consumer, and explicit enqueue candidates. They do not cover the ordinary
RX stamp, pending first-peer identity, target compile, module installation or
runtime. See the expanded hashes, callsites, and outputs in
`docs/evidence/WR1200JS-FT-RX-QUEUE-PROVENANCE-2026-11-19.json`.

No firmware source changed. Prepared FT remains uninstalled pending a tested
BSS+MAC pending-generation lifecycle and the IAPP completion contract.

## Chosen FT first-peer identity policy — 2026-11-19

The owner chose to preserve native first-peer BT_REQ behavior with a bounded
pending BSS+MAC identity ledger. Added a standalone C helper and Nim model for
reference sharing, invalidation, stale-token refusal, safe slot reuse and
per-slot overflow poisoning. The C fixture passes under ASan/UBSan with GNU89
`-Wall -Wextra -Werror`; `nim c -r tools/iot/ft_pending_identity_check.nim`
passes. These are model/helper checks only; the ledger is not connected to the
adapter, queues, association table or FT handler.

Pinned `mlme.c` also shows restart drains queued elements, while
`MlmeQueueDestroy` resets queue indices without per-element callbacks and lacks
an adapter argument. Integration must explicitly release/invalidate ledger
references for normal dispatch, stale dequeue, enqueue failure, restart drain
and destroy; it must atomically authorize target-BSS insertion. Exact callsites,

## Remote key-response payload trace — 2026-11-19

Pinned remote-side FT_KDP_KeyRequestToUs calls FT_QueryKeyInfoForKDP on the
received FT_KDP_EVT_KEY_ELM, then emits that same block in KEY_RSP_AUTO.
The inspected query reads KeyInfo.R1KHID and does not reference S1KHID; it
fills PMK/key-response fields. The local daemon forwards the received response
to every Wi-Fi interface. MAC, S1KHID and R1KHID may assist routing but are
not per-attempt generation identifiers: delayed retries with identical identities
remain indistinguishable. These observations do not establish encryption or
peer authenticity. No safe nonce/generation protocol is inferred from them.
Durable daemon-source report now includes remote-driver hashes and references.

## Pinned IAPP daemon response trace — 2026-11-19

Read actual c25283e archive members trunk/user/ralinkiappd/rtmpiapp.c,
rtmpiapp.h and rt_config.h. Their SHA256 and exact source anchors are in
WR1200JS-FT-IAPP-DAEMON-RESPONSE-SOURCE-2026-11-19.json. Automatic request and
ack events call SecurityBlockSend/Ack. Each builds and zeroes a new frame then
copies event payload into SB; those functions do not copy request InitVec into
ack. On receiving ACK, daemon packages received InitVec plus SB into
RT_SET_FT_KEY_RSP and submits it to ALL registered Wi-Fi interfaces. Thus the
receiving ioctl interface alone cannot establish original BSS. Source inspected
so far does not establish an echoed per-request nonce or generation; do not
assume either. Optional encryption and remote key-request/response construction
still require tracing before designing a correlation protocol.

## 2026-11-01 Sol: offline-channel teardown cannot reuse ring free

Checked the exact Linux 4.4.198 target header: `pci_channel_offline()` is only
`pdev->error_state != pci_channel_io_normal`; it does not cover every physical
link disappearance. PCI error recovery offers `error_detected`, `mmio_enabled`,
`link_reset`, `slot_reset`, and `resume`, but registering these callbacks alone
does not prove DMA stopped or provide a general surprise-removal cleanup receipt.

Inspected both conditional implementations in merged
`common/cmm_mac_pci.c::RTMPFreeTxRxRingMemory`. The actual WR1200JS target TU
command defines `RESOURCE_PRE_ALLOC`, so its selected function frees descriptor
and preallocated DMA buffers without the non-prealloc implementation's ring
index MMIO reads. However the paired `RTMPResetTxRxRingMemory()` selected by
`RESOURCE_PRE_ALLOC` unmaps/releases streaming TX and RX packets and reads
descriptor contents. Also, the non-prealloc implementation still has three
hardware index reads and streaming unmaps. Thus offline cleanup must select the
exact effective config and cannot call reset/reclaim routines that consult
device state or unmap buffers whose DMA ownership was not revoked. The
ordinary teardown calls ring reset/free through `hif_sys_exit`, close, and
adapter destruction. `RtmpOSIRQRelease` calls `synchronize_irq` before
`free_irq`, but is reached only through deeper teardown and is not an
adapter-wide producer fence. Neither an offline check nor skipping a few MMIO
reads provides a safe release path.

Next implementation must add an explicit teardown contract across all ring
free callers: normal close retains existing semantics only after device-
specific DMA idle/readback; terminal bus removal must first establish hardware
isolation (or a platform-guaranteed DMA revocation boundary), fence every
producer and IRQ, join callbacks, then reclaim software ring ownership without
MMIO, with exact streaming-DMA unmap and descriptor lifetime semantics.
If this board/platform cannot establish that isolation on physical loss, the
driver must not claim safe reclamation there; keep that event distinct from
controlled PCI unbind. No code bypass added; no device action.

## 2026-11-01 Sol: PCI core/API boundary checked against Linux 4.4

Verified target headers use `void (*remove)(struct pci_dev *)` and expose
`pci_clear_master()`, `pci_disable_device()`, `pci_channel_offline()` and PCI
error-recovery handlers. Pinned Linux v4.4 `pci_device_remove()` calls the
driver's remove callback, then `pcibios_free_irq()`, then clears the driver
pointer; it does not automatically
call `pci_clear_master()` there. The kernel PCI API defines `pci_clear_master`
as clearing the bus-master bit, but that alone is not a receipt that already
issued transactions completed. The PCI error-recovery documentation says the
platform may isolate I/O and notify `error_detected`, but its interrupt section
explicitly does not guarantee delivery has stopped. Thus: no core-veto path,
no automatic bus-master cleanup guarantee at unbind, and no portable physical
loss receipt are available to this driver without target host-controller
evidence. Current WR1200JS effective config also has PCIe port service/AER,
hotplug and IOMMU disabled. Exact target `.config` checks are evidence; source
does not include the host PCI controller implementation, so MT7621 isolation
and reset boundary remain unproven. No candidate change based on assumed core
behavior. No router access or mutation.

or self-cancel deadlock and requires caller-context audit. With
RTMP_TIMER_TASK_SUPPORT, RtmpTimerQThread pops a node under TimerQLock then calls
handle outside it and may rearm Repeat/State; RtmpTimerQRemove only scans queued
nodes and does not join an executing handler. Therefore ordinary release/queue
removal is not sufficient acceptance proof for freeing failed peer resources.

Next process-context per-entry retirement with rearm fence, executing timer-task
callback ownership and unconditional direct-timer synchronization after releasing
MAC/IRQ/transition locks; only then timer/resource-specific cleanup and counters.
Do not add automatic SET_ENTRY_NONE/free based on current timer return value.

## Close ordering and MMIO availability — 2026-10-22

Linux clears netif_running before ndo_stop (dev.c:1394,1402,1417-1418), but stale
recovery still needs shared final restart/disable protocol. BcnRingLock already
exists; BH/IRQ macros differ by effective config. Do not hold across polls.

   next task. Never assume GitHub authentication transfers with the folder.

### IoT deferred reset retry liveness — 2026-10-24

Source evidence `docs/evidence/WR1200JS-IOT-562-RESET-RETRY-WORKER-LIVENESS-2026-10-24.md`
records that retry is tied to periodic `RTPCICmdThread` command processing. The
pinned worker can exit on `RtmpOSTaskWait` failure, sets HALT, and clears queued
commands; init failure and halt stop timers/MLME and call task exit. This means
no eventual reset drain is proven after the retry worker disappears. Radio state
remains not-ready while pending, so this is an unresolved liveness/teardown gap,
not proof of device failure. Next trace reset entry paths through suspend, worker
wait failure and adapter teardown, then define lifetime-safe completion or
fail-closed teardown and test the interleavings. No production code/image/router
was changed for this audit. Preserve existing dirty files.

Close-path follow-up completed by Sol: staged `wr_iot_drv_close_checked` is
not wired in place of legacy `rt28xx_close`; outer lifetime retention remains
unproven. Its success is software close completion, not proof of hardware/RF
quiescence, yet the transition helper clears `reset_pending` on successful
`WR_RADIO_CLOSE`. Do not treat this as a safe terminal reset path or wire it to
production until the whole close/PM/error caller chain, hardware quiescence and
adapter lifetime are established. Evidence 562 records the finding. This turn
was source inspection only; no tests/build/CI/router operation. Continue from
the unresolved lifetime-safe teardown/drain design; preserve dirty files.

PM follow-up from pinned source `c25283e915a2a00a763774dd255b14aff997285e`:
`pci_main_dev.c:80-123` suspend calls `RTMP_DRIVER_PCI_SUSPEND`, then
`rt28xx_close`, then disables PCI. The legacy close invokes void `RTMPDrvClose`
and returns 0 even if `RT28xxPciAsicRadioOff` failed; that failure is only
logged. The candidate's periodic reset retry is therefore removed before PCI
power-down, and close success is not evidence of radio quiescence. Evidence
562 has the exact caller trace. Next design a lifetime-safe reset owner spanning
RTNL deferral, worker exit, suspend/resume and teardown; retain pending intent
and deny READY until verified recovery. No implementation, test/build/CI or
router action this audit. Preserve dirty files; Sol remains sole writer.

Teardown owner confirmed at pinned revision: PCI remove calls `RtmpPhyNetDevExit`
then `RtmpRaDevCtrlExit`; the latter calls `RTMPFreeAdapter`, which frees adapter
locks/resources and memory. The candidate's `adapter-free.inc` assumes callers
already quiesced work; it does not cancel or join a retry executor. Evidence 562
now records the lifecycle requirement: initialize before any cleanup path,
prevent enqueue after retirement, synchronously drain/cancel before free, use
nonblocking RTNL in worker, preserve pending reset while PCI is suspended, and
only resume BSS admission after verified recovery. Continue by deriving the
state transitions and caller ordering before integrating a workqueue. No code,
test, build, CI or router changes this turn.

Exact resume order is now in evidence 562: PCI D0/restore/enable, device attach,
`rt28xx_open`, PCI-resume notification, then queue wake. The transition candidate
does not bind to that PM callback, and `rt28xx_open` is driver init, not radio
verification. Next settle how queues and BSS admission remain fail-closed until
pending reset/readback completes, and whether attach must move or can remain
gated. Only then implement the PM-bound owner/workqueue lifecycle.

### IoT isolated suspend/resume transition model — 2026-10-24

Sol added candidate-only PM states and helpers in `tools/iot/radio-transition.h`
and race cases in `tools/iot/check-radio-transition.c`. Suspend fences new
operations, preserves reset kinds across an in-flight RESET/PM window, and
requires all tickets to retire before marking SUSPENDED. Resume starts
UNVERIFIED; reset/readback gates BSS admission. Strict local MinGW C11 compile
and both transition/reset-admission fixtures passed. Local ASan/UBSan link was
unavailable (`libasan` and `libubsan` missing). No CI, target/MIPS build, router
or production-driver integration.

Pinned callback audit: device PM suspend/resume and remove use `device_lock`,
but PCI PM calls `rt28xx_close/open` directly rather than via RTNL-asserting
netdev open/stop. Resume calls `netif_device_attach` before `rt28xx_open`, and
the kernel helper wakes TX queues for a running netdev. The current candidate
does not gate packet TX; this makes attach/queue safety an explicit blocker.
The device lock alone does not drain the proposed retry worker. Further pinned
source: main, MBSS, AP-client, WDS and monitor netdevs share
`rt28xx_send_packets`, whose running check only reads `IFF_UP`; direct PCI
close does not invoke their stop callbacks. Moving main attach later leaves
virtual-interface TX exposed. Evidence 562 now includes an ordering contract
for adapter-wide TX admission/drain, all-netdev quiescence, worker cancellation,
checked close, and fail-closed resume.

Limits remain: sequential model only; no proof of driver callback integration,
worker cancellation/liveness, adapter lifetime, queue/TX gating or radio-off.
Do not wire it into the driver yet. Next: prove virtual-netdev enumeration and
active-TX drain/lock ordering, then implement a separate candidate for the PM

effects through abort, then complete config-owner lifecycle/ID budget/data gate.

## Sol: AP auto-channel/startup scope narrows, but does not open, IoT admission

Audited the checked candidate source path and retained
`WR1200JS-AP-STARTUP-COMMAND-SCOPE.md`.  On AP auto-channel boot,
`rtmp_init_inf.c` enables PCI interrupt and `RTMPEnableRxTx()` before channel
selection and before `APStartUp()`.  `APStartUp()` later reaches EDCA/slot time,
direct-MMIO RDG/WTBL, internal command-thread protection, rates, beacons,
sync/pre-TBTT and Band Steering.  EDCA/slot are the relevant no-response MCU
operations and remain retained as active intents; direct MMIO or internal
command-thread work must not be mislabelled as an Andes ACK dependency.

Consequently neither an `APStartUp()`-adjacent finish nor a first-open-only
shortcut is acceptable: the former is too late for automatic-channel Rx/Tx,
and the rescan thread calls `APStop()` then `APStartUp()` again.  No bootstrap
gate was opened and no normal data admission, image or runtime claim was made.
Next: bind the task-pinned configuration owner and mandatory failure/abandon
path into real outer init, account the checked-ID budget by actual branch, and
derive a pre-RxTx release condition without changing channel settings.  The
new audit is source-only; the previous target evidence still applies only to
its exact candidate SHA.  Owner `docs/reference/` untouched.

## Sol: outer init now owns config begin/abandon; success is intentionally not admission

Added `mcu-config-init-owner` after timing in the peer82 CI generation chain.
After successful `MCUSysInit`, it snapshots the boot ticket and begins the
task-pinned configuration owner. Any later error funnels through `err6`, which
abandon-finishes that owner before `MCUSysExit`; an earlier MCUSys failure never
has an owner to release. The normal-tail success finish is attempted, but then
intentionally enters `err8`, so no normal command/data admission or production
open is implied. An active EDCA/slot intent therefore refuses success and
follows the same retained-failure cleanup.

Fresh isolated regeneration through all preceding layers, owner ASan/UBSan and
the new ordering check passed. This is source/host evidence only; it does not
prove the target compile, image, response/order of no-response firmware calls,
or device runtime. Next work: derive a real execution proof or safe supported
policy for timing intents, then establish an outer release condition before
auto-channel Rx/Tx. Do not remove the final refusal meanwhile. Owner
`docs/reference/` untouched.

## Sol: transport completion cannot substitute for firmware receipt

Fresh source audit of the retained MT7603 PCI command path establishes that
EDCA/slot-time use no-wait messages: sequence zero, no ACK wait, callback or
firmware-result storage. `AndesSendCmdMsg()` reports attempted kickout; PCI
TX completion later only moves the host buffer to `tx_doneq` for freeing.
Neither event proves MCU consumption or execution.  Retained timing intents
must therefore continue to block configuration finish and the closed IoT gate;
do not treat DMA/TX completion as ACK.  Evidence:
`docs/evidence/WR1200JS-NORESPONSE-TRANSPORT-BOUNDARY.md`.  No router/image
claim or mutation.  Continue only with a documented command-specific ordered
receipt, or a safe policy that preserves this boundary.
